references.text: God tests his people to know their heart, the same theme of divine testing as in Exodus 20:20
God's testing of the people to see if they love him with all their heart
Fear of the Lord leads to obedience and blessing
Fearing the Lord is linked to walking in his ways and not sinning
God tested Abraham; the same Hebrew word 'נַסָּה' is used for divine testing
Fear of the Lord keeps people away from sin
Fear God and keep his commandments - summarizes the relationship between reverence for God and obedience
The Lord is the one to be feared, not humans
Serve God with reverence, for our God is a consuming fire - links reverence for God to worship
Live in reverence during their time as foreigners - reverence as motivation for holy living
Perfect love casts out fear, but reverence for God remains
Both use "Do not be afraid!" to lead the people from panic to a right relationship with God (salvation versus reverence).
Complementary scenes in the theology of the Exodus: Deliverance from Egypt (13) leads to testing and reverence at Sinai (20).
A clear theological parallel: "Do not be afraid!" used as a correction of the people's attitude toward God after or during sin/crisis.
Recurring motif: God uses "testing" as an educational tool to shape obedience and reverence.
Complementary purposes of the Sinai revelation: to create faith in the prophet (19) and reverence for God among the people (20).
